obligation: Processor notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the payment processor (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10 (N71-R04)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data taken through the owner's merchant account, including a skimming script on the owner's web pages or a common point of purchase notice from the processor
deadline: Immediately, and no later than 24 hours after suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term). Clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation
notify: Processor's risk team (number on the printed contact list)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1 - card brand rule applied through the processor, not law
trigger: Discovery of evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that handles it
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery; in practice reported through the processor
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations via the processor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Visa Level 3 merchant by Visa's table (about 2,000 Visa transactions a year)

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.2
trigger: After notifying Visa
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa
notify: Visa and the processor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.4
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
deadline: Within 3 calendar days; the processor can extract the card numbers used during the window of exposure
notify: Visa (via the processor)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the owner holds no card numbers; the processor provides them

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.5
trigger: Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator (PFI)
deadline: Initial forensic report within 5 business days after the PFI contract is signed; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation. The PFI must not have served the entity in the past 3 years
notify: Visa and the processor (the PFI reports directly to Visa)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Visa requires it

citation: Mastercard, American Express, and Discover operating rules - applied through the processor, not law
trigger: Suspected compromise of those brands' card data
deadline: Per processor and brand instructions (not verified here)
notify: Processor; card brands through the processor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow processor instructions; these rules were not verified

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with a card number and any required security code, and a user name or email address with a password for an online account (501.171(1)(g)). Names, emails, phones, and order history alone are not personal information under this definition
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days if good cause is given to the Department of Legal Affairs in writing within the 30 days, 501.171(3)(a); the extension applies only to this notice to individuals)
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email (501.171(4)(d))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for skimmed card data with security codes; a patron export alone does not trigger it

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in a written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the owner reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document the determination in writing, keep it at least 5 years, and give it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for skimmed card data; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (a skimmer running through one on-sale could reach that)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the owner (inbound)
trigger: The ticketing vendor, processor, or another vendor has a breach of a system it maintains for the owner
deadline: No later than 10 days following the vendor's determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; the owner then gives the notices above
notify: The owner
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the owner remains responsible for the notices even if the vendor sends them (501.171(6)(b))

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of each state where affected individuals reside (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 15% of buyers live outside Florida; counsel applies each state's law, and some states' definitions may cover data that Florida's does not

trigger: Account takeover, payout fraud, or card skimming
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0 to 2); the bank needs a report number to try to recall a diverted payout
notify: FBI (IC3 online report) and local police
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy terms
notify: Carrier claims line
applies_at_this_tier: No - no cyber policy; the general liability policy excludes data breach costs (read 2026-07-30)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment (for example a demand not to publish the patron export)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a Nevada gaming licensee
deadline: Notify the Chair within 24 hours of activating the incident response plan; Initial Cybersecurity Incident Response report within 5 calendar days; written updates every 30 days; investigation report available on request
notify: Chair of the Nevada Gaming Control Board
applies_at_this_tier: No - no gaming license and no Nevada operations (N71-R01)

trigger: Suspicious activity at a casino or card club
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection of facts that may be a basis for filing
notify: FinCEN
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a casino or card club (N71-R03)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the owner holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the owner holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
